observations.verdict: 72 between-eval views ALSO fit at headroom=16

conclusion: For the 4B MTP workload, the between-eval view count (and their metadata footprint) fits even within the stock 16-view headroom. The 16->80 increase therefore does not change the pass/fail outcome for this specific workload; it widens the capacity margin (consistent with the (C) boundary test's ~5x N_max ratio: 44->222 @S=1024, 89->445 @S=2048). The patch is a headroom increase that raises the ceiling for larger/more views; the 4B MTP graph's ~72 views are small enough to fit under the stock bound. No perf regression from the patch (patched is actually faster: 98.3 vs 76.5 gen t/s).
residual: A workload with a larger per-view metadata footprint (or a larger view count) would be the case where the 16-view bound is binding. The (C) hardware-free boundary test is the direct capacity proof; the (D) hardware lane confirms the patch is benign (no regression, no correctness issue) on a real recurrent/MTP graph and that the 4B MTP workload is not the binding case.
